title: Cap salary outliers (quantile) — cap_outliers_salary
text: data data.frame containing data. col Character string. Name column process (default "salary_in_usd"). lower Probability lower quantile (0 1, default 0.01). upper Probability upper quantile (0 1, default 0.99). clip_side Capping strategy: "" (default), "upper" "lower". na_rm Logical. NA values ignored computing quantiles? (default TRUE) verbose Logical. TRUE, prints summary replacements performed.

title: Cap salary outliers (quantile) — cap_outliers_salary
text: data.frame target column modified (extreme values replaced corresponding quantile bounds).

title: Cap salary outliers (quantile) — cap_outliers_salary
text: function computes two bounds, L (lower) U (upper), corresponding requested quantile probabilities. Values L replaced L, values U replaced U. can choose whether cap tails, upper tail, lower tail.

title: Cap salary outliers (quantile) — cap_outliers_salary
code: # Simple data with an extreme salary value (1 million) df <- data.frame(   salary_in_usd = c(50000, 55000, 60000, 45000, 1000000) )  # Cap the upper 10% (winsorisation) df_capped <- cap_outliers_salary(df, lower = 0.1, upper = 0.9, clip_side = "upper") #> Error in cap_outliers_salary(df, lower = 0.1, upper = 0.9, clip_side = "upper"): could not find function "cap_outliers_salary"  # The value 1,000,000 is replaced by the 90th percentile print(df_capped) #> Error: object 'df_capped' not found

title: Convert salaries to USD — convert_currency_to_usd
text: data data.frame must contain least following columns: salary: gross amount local currency. salary_currency: ISO code currency (e.g. "EUR", "GBP"). work_year: reference fiscal year. salary_in_usd: (Optional, overwritten/created).

title: Convert salaries to USD — convert_currency_to_usd
text: data.frame enriched computed salary_in_usd column.

title: Convert salaries to USD — convert_currency_to_usd
text: conversion procedure follows: Validation: Checks columns salary, salary_currency work_year present. Typing: Ensures salary numeric year integer. Join: Merges data reference table exchange_rates_to_usd based currency year. Computation: Applies exchange rate update salary_in_usd. Cleanup: Removes temporary rate columns (rate).

title: Convert salaries to USD — convert_currency_to_usd
text: function depends global object exchange_rates_to_usd, must contain columns currency, year rate.

title: Convert salaries to USD — convert_currency_to_usd
code: # For the example to work, we simulate the exchange rate table # Normally, this object 'exchange_rates_to_usd' is loaded in the package exchange_rates_to_usd <- data.frame(   currency = c("EUR", "GBP"),   year = c(2023, 2023),   rate = c(1.1, 1.25) # 1 EUR = 1.1 USD )  df <-  data.frame(   salary = 60000,   salary_currency = "GBP",   salary_in_usd = 75000,   work_year = 2023 )  # Conversion convert_currency_to_usd(df) #> Error in convert_currency_to_usd(df): could not find function "convert_currency_to_usd"

title: Enforce simple column types — enforce_types
text: algorithm processes data column column: Ignores columns already numeric, factors dates. Trims surrounding whitespace trimws. Numeric conversion: proportion values can converted numeric exceeds num_threshold, column converted numeric (integer possible). Factor conversion: Otherwise, number unique values less equal max_factor_levels, column converted factor. Otherwise, column remains character.

title: Enforce simple column types — enforce_types
code: df <- data.frame(   id = c("1", "2", "3"),              # Should become integer   cat = c("A", "A", "B"),             # Should become factor   text = c("Unique1", "Unique2", "Unique3"), # Remains character   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  str(df) # All columns are character initially #> 'data.frame':	3 obs. of  3 variables: #>  $ id  : chr  "1" "2" "3" #>  $ cat : chr  "A" "A" "B" #>  $ text: chr  "Unique1" "Unique2" "Unique3"  df_typed <- enforce_types(df, max_factor_levels = 2) str(df_typed) # Types corrected #> 'data.frame':	3 obs. of  3 variables: #>  $ id  : int  1 2 3 #>  $ cat : Factor w/ 2 levels "A","B": 1 1 2 #>  $ text: chr  "Unique1" "Unique2" "Unique3"

title: Export data to CSV — export_csv
text: function simplifies CSV export performing following steps: Check data object data.frame. Create path directory recursively already exist. Append .csv extension file name missing. Choose optimised writing function based separator: sep = ";": use utils::write.csv2 (European-style format). sep = ",": use utils::write.csv (US-style format). Otherwise: use utils::write.table.

title: Export data to CSV — export_csv
code: # Test data df_test <- data.frame(   id = 1:3,   name = c("Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"),   score = c(10.5, 15.2, 8.0) )  # Create a temporary folder to avoid writing on your disk tmp_folder <- tempfile() # Use a random folder name  # 1. Simple export (semicolon separator by default) path_file <- export_csv(df_test, path = tmp_folder, filename = "test_export") #> Error in export_csv(df_test, path = tmp_folder, filename = "test_export"): could not find function "export_csv"  # Check that the file exists file.exists(path_file) #> Error: object 'path_file' not found  # 2. Export with comma separator and no overwrite (should error if rerun) try({   export_csv(df_test, path = tmp_folder, filename = "test_export", sep = ",", overwrite = FALSE) }) #> Error in export_csv(df_test, path = tmp_folder, filename = "test_export",  :  #>   could not find function "export_csv"  # Clean up temporary folder unlink(tmp_folder, recursive = TRUE)

NULL (default), columns processed. exclude Optional character vector column names exclude processing. num_method Method numeric columns: "median", "mean" "constant". cat_method Method character/factor columns: "mode", "constant" "new_level". num_constant Value used num_method = "constant" (default 0). cat_constant Value used cat_method = "constant" (default "Missing"). verbose Logical. title: Impute missing values for numeric and categorical columns — impute_missing
text: strategy applied depends column type: Numeric (numeric, integer): "median" (default): Replace median (robust outliers). "mean": Replace mean. "constant": Replace value supplied num_constant (e.g. 0). Categorical (character, factor): "mode" (default): Replace frequent value. case ties, alphabetical order used. "constant" "new_level": Replace value cat_constant (default "Missing"). Note: column factor, levels automatically updated include new value needed. Logical (logical): Replace majority value (TRUE FALSE).

TRUE (default) remove rows failing validate_ranges needed columns present. ranges_min_year, ranges_max_year Bounds passed validate_ranges. impute_verbose Logical, forwarded impute_missing. cat_constant Value used imputing categorical columns "new_level" strategy.

title: Validate value ranges — validate_ranges
text: function applies strict filter. row kept following conditions TRUE: salary > 0 remote_ratio 0 100 inclusive work_year min_year max_year none values NA message printed console rows removed.

title: Validate value ranges — validate_ranges
code: # Data with an invalid row (negative salary and remote_ratio > 100) df <- data.frame(   salary = c(50000, -100, 60000),   remote_ratio = c(50, 150, 100),   work_year = c(2022, 2022, 2023) )  # Apply the filter df_clean <- validate_ranges(df) #> Error in validate_ranges(df): could not find function "validate_ranges"  # Result: only valid rows are kept nrow(df_clean) # Should be 2 #> Error: object 'df_clean' not found

text: Check whether data.frame contains columns required subsequent processing.

title: Validate presence of required columns — validate_schema
code: validate_schema(dataframe, required_columns, boolean_form = FALSE)

title: Validate presence of required columns — validate_schema
text: dataframe data.frame check. required_columns character vector names required columns. boolean_form Logical (TRUE/FALSE). TRUE, returns simple boolean. FALSE, returns detailed message.

title: Validate presence of required columns — validate_schema
text: boolean_form = TRUE: boolean. boolean_form = FALSE: character string (success error message).

title: Validate presence of required columns — validate_schema
text: function supports two output modes via boolean_form argument: Boolean mode: Returns TRUE FALSE. Useful inside conditions. Verbose mode (default): Returns text message explicitly listing missing columns, confirming required columns present.

title: Validate presence of required columns — validate_schema
code: df <- data.frame(id = 1:3, salary = c(100, 200, 300))  # Success case (message) validate_schema(df, c("id", "salary")) #> [1] "All required colums are present in the dataframe"  # Failure case (message) validate_schema(df, c("id", "salary", "age")) #> [1] "The dataframe in not complete and it's missing age"  # Success case (boolean) if (validate_schema(df, c("id"), boolean_form = TRUE)) {   print("All required columns are present.") } #> Error in validate_schema(df, c("id"), boolean_form = TRUE): unused argument (boolean_form = TRUE)

title: Write a cleaning report to a text file — write_cleaning_report
code: # Raw data df_raw <- data.frame(id = 1:5, val = c(10, NA, 30, 1000, 50))  # Cleaned data (example) df_clean <- data.frame(id = c(1, 3, 4, 5), val = c(10, 30, 100, 50))  # List of operations performed (collected during the script) my_stats <- list(   "NA imputed" = 1,   "Outliers capped" = 1,   "Rows removed" = 1 )  # Generate the report tmp_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt") write_cleaning_report(df_clean, original_data = df_raw, file = tmp_file, stats_list = my_stats) #> Error in write_cleaning_report(df_clean, original_data = df_raw, file = tmp_file,     stats_list = my_stats): could not find function "write_cleaning_report"  # Read the result cat(readLines(tmp_file), sep = "\n") #> Warning: cannot open file '/var/folders/0f/_fg7x2451bj2lywhltbl4j3w0000gn/T//RtmpwhCryX/fileb1b8779c004d.txt': No such file or directory #> Error in file(con, "r"): cannot open the connection
